Cauchy–Schwarz bounds chord perturbation by c√(2Σn²r^{2n−2})|z−w| and derivative min singular value similarly. S(r)=r²(4−3r²+r⁴)/(1−r²)^3 strictly increases. The explicit two-sided harmonic shear with balanced ± coefficients saturates the vertical directional derivative at real r and has exact boundary norm; at critical R its Jacobian is zero, Lewy's nonzero-Jacobian theorem for locally injective harmonic maps forbids any larger universal injectivity radius. At r≥R the co-Lipschitz infimum is zero; M=1 identity. Check normalizations, open ball endpoints, all r<1, and coefficient-series convergence. Finite code is corroborative only.
